name: 1403 Vintage Mono Pro
classification_notes: An all-uppercase monospace built on the print-chain glyph shapes of the IBM 1403 mainframe line printer, with small capitals standing in for lowercase.
summary: An all-caps monospace revival of the IBM 1403 line printer's print-chain glyphs, expanded to over 2,300 characters across four scripts.
description: 1403 Vintage Mono Pro started as a weekend attempt to recreate the 52 characters of the IBM 1403 printer's A and H print chains, and grew into a full multiscript monospace covering Latin (including Vietnamese), Cyrillic, Greek and Hebrew. It carries real technical depth for a novelty-sounding premise, with extensive OpenType support for fractions, superscripts and locale variants.
foundry_blurb: Slanted Hall describe it as inspired by the IBM 1403 mainframe line printer, expanded from an initial 52 characters to over 2,300 glyphs supporting most Latin-alphabet languages plus Cyrillic, Greek and Hebrew.

name: 1403 Vintage Mono Limited
classification_notes: A pared-back Latin-only subset of 1403 Vintage Mono Pro, keeping the same all-uppercase line-printer construction.
summary: The budget, Latin-only edition of 1403 Vintage Mono Pro, keeping its line-printer character at a fraction of the glyph count.
description: 1403 Vintage Mono Limited strips the Pro version back to the original A and H print-chain characters plus a basic Latin set, small capitals still standing in for lowercase. It's the entry point into the same IBM 1403-inspired design for buyers who don't need the multiscript Pro version.
foundry_blurb: Slanted Hall describe it as including the original 52 characters making up the A and H chains, along with the basic complement of Latin characters, pointing to the Pro version for broader language support.
